definition: The structured supportvector machine is a machine learning algorithm that generalizes the support vector machine (SVM) classifier.
details: Whereas the SVM classifier supports binary classification, multiclass classification and regression, the structured SVM allows training of a classifier for general structured output labels. As an example, a sample instance might be a natural language sentence, and the output label is an annotated parse tree. Training a classifier consists of showing pairs of correct sample and output label pairs. After training, the structured SVM model allows one to predict for new sample instances the corresponding output label; that is, given a natural language sentence, the classifier can produce the most likely parse tree.

explainer.lead: A machine learning algorithm that generalizes the SVM classifier to general structured output labels. It matters because many tasks produce structured labels, like parse trees, not just class labels.

tiers.eli5: Like a sorting machine that usually drops items into single bins, but here it assembles a whole labelled diagram for each item.
tiers.practitioner: Training shows pairs of correct samples and output labels, after which the model predicts labels for new samples; the pitfall is the computational cost that comes with large structured output spaces.
tiers.paperLevel: Generalizes the SVM classifier, which supports binary classification, multiclass classification and regression, to training a classifier for general structured output labels; after training on sample-label pairs it predicts labels for new instances.

explainer.example: A natural language sentence is the sample and an annotated parse tree is the output label; the trained model predicts the parse tree for a new sentence.
